title: Even part in the first coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{\pm1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. The even part of $f$ in its first coordinate is the function on $\{\pm1\}^n$ given by $x\mapsto \bigl(f(1,x)+f(-1,x)\bigr)/2$, where the first-coordinate slices are evaluated at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube to the real numbers
